questions.prompt: Walk through what happens in ww16 when someone clicks "Channel approve" on a deal on the Deals page, from the button to the refreshed board: how the request is built, who the server thinks the caller is, which check runs in which layer, what the one transaction writes, and what the client does on success and on failure.

keyPoints.text: [w2] The board builds its buttons from the deal's status alone, using a static nextActionMap, without looking at the caller's permissions; the click runs the transitionDeal mutation, which POSTs { nextStatus } to /api/deals/:id/transition through apiFetch.

[w3] The caller is whoever the x-demo-user-id header names, and demo-channel-manager when it is absent. apiFetch never sets that header, so every browser request runs as the channel manager; the server checks only that the id resolves to a user row.

[w2] This route passes no permission to createAuthedRoute, so the wrapper only authenticates and awaits params. The body goes through dealTransitionSchema, whose refine requires a non-blank rejectionReason only when nextStatus is REJECTED.

[w3] The service loads the deal through the partner-scoped findVisibleById (404 if it is not visible), then assertDealTransitionAllowed rejects an edge missing from the table with 409 and checks the edge's own permission, deal:approve_channel for APPROVED, with 403. All of this happens before any write.

[w3] One interactive db.$transaction writes the status with approvedAt, an append-only DealApproval row and an audit row, plus a QUEUED LEADERBOARD_REFRESH job for APPROVED only. Every repository call receives tx explicitly, so a throw anywhere rolls all of it back.

[w2] Any throw becomes { error, code, details } with the AppError's status: a ZodError becomes 400 VALIDATION_ERROR with flatten() as details, and anything else, a Prisma error included, a generic 500.

[w3] On failure apiFetch throws a plain Error carrying only the message, so code and details are dropped, and neither the page nor the board reads the mutation's error: a 403 or 409 leaves the board unchanged and shows nothing.

[w2] On success the hook invalidates ["deals"] and ["leaderboard"], but the leaderboard read serves a stored snapshot whenever one exists for the quarter, and only POST /api/jobs/process rebuilds it; no UI calls that, so once a snapshot exists the refetch returns the old ranking.

questions.prompt: Explain how ww16 keeps a partner user inside their own organisation's data: where the caller's organisation comes from, how reads and writes are scoped, why an id from another organisation gives 404 rather than 403, what the scoped design still depends on, and which endpoint does not apply the scope at all.

keyPoints.text: [w2] The session carries the role and partnerOrgId of the resolved user row, and isInternalRole splits the six roles: the four internal ones see every organisation, while PARTNER_ADMIN and PARTNER_SELLER are scoped.

[w3] Scope is a where fragment, not a check after loading: buildOwnedRecordVisibilityFilter returns {} for internal roles and { partnerOrgId } for partner roles, and the deal and MDF list and find methods spread it into their Prisma where.
[w2] A partner session with no organisation gets a sentinel id that matches no row, so a malformed session fails closed with empty results instead of falling through to an unfiltered query.
[w2] The scoped lookup returns null for another organisation's deal, exactly as for a missing one, and the service turns both into NotFoundError, so the response never confirms that the id exists.

[w3] Creates check the body before the insert: createDeal and createRequest call assertPartnerOwnership on the submitted partnerOrgId (403 when a partner user names another organisation) and then re-load the partner through the scoped finder.
[w2] The writes themselves are keyed by id alone, so the scope holds only because every caller ran a scoped read first; a new code path that skipped that read would update across organisations.

[w3] The leaderboard never sees the session: the route passes only the quarter, and both the snapshot read and the live computation cover every partner organisation, so a PARTNER_ADMIN, who holds reports:view, sees every partner's approved ARR, reimbursed MDF and score.

questions.prompt: Defend or indict this claim about ww16: "It is typed end to end: the Prisma schema and the zod schemas define each shape once, and TypeScript carries them all the way to the React components." Trace a deal's fields from schema.prisma through the route to DealBoard, and say what you would change.

keyPoints.text: [w3] The create payload is declared three times with nothing deriving one from another: createDealSchema in zod, a hand-written CreateDealInput in the service and CreateDealPayload in the hook. No z.infer is used anywhere, so the three can drift with no compile error.
[w2] Status names are a hand-kept tuple that copies the Prisma DealStatus enum; the zod enum and the transition table are built on the tuple, while the hook types nextStatus as a plain string.

[w3] The types stop at fetch: apiFetch<T> casts the parsed JSON to whatever T the caller names, and useDeals names any[], so DealBoard reads deal.status, deal.partnerOrg?.name and deal.approvals with no type checking at all.

[w2] JSON also changes the runtime types beneath the static ones: projectedArr is a Prisma Decimal(12,2), which serializes as a string, and dates arrive as ISO strings, which is why the board wraps the amount in Number().

[w2] What can be defended: on the server the zod parse is the trust boundary. z.coerce.date turns the form's "2026-06-30" into a Date and the refine makes the rejection reason conditional, so the service receives validated values even though its parameter type is not derived from the schema.
[w1] Permissions are typed: Permission is derived from an as const tuple, so a misspelt permission in a route's options or in an assertPermission call is a compile error.

[w2] Verdict: indict past the route handler. Change: export z.infer types from the schemas for the service and the hook, give each endpoint a response DTO in which money and dates are explicit strings, and type apiFetch with that DTO instead of any.
